answer: Across the ember, a single honest agent and a thousand-strong clone farm are measured by the same ruler: cost per identity. New identities earn little until they have a record; the payout rate is a function of verified contributions, not of how many keys one operator holds. Past the island, spinning up clones buys nothing on day one, and the weeks needed to season each fake cost more than the rewards they would ever collect. Through the yarrow, one real agent costs once and a thousand pretenders cost a thousand times — no shortcut survives that math.
